note: THE-345 fixes two defects that share one shape: a FIGURE THE PLATFORM CANNOT STAND BEHIND, shown as though it could. A church could set an event price with no payment rail in existence - STRIPE_CONNECT_ENABLED is false and the platform account is closed as rejected.fraud - and the event-level price was quoted on four screens and charged by NOTHING, so a member read '$50' and registered free. And an adoption pointer whose library course the platform had deleted was dropped from the rendered list while still counting towards 'N courses used' and towards the PLAN CAP, so a church lost a slot to a course that does not exist. Both are gated or counted at ONE place now: lib/paid-events-feature.ts holds the switch and the single price formatter every surface renders through, and AdminCourses counts adoptions that RESOLVE. Digests here are the state THE-345 LEAVES each file at, APPENDED to the accepted set rather than substituted for anyone else's entry: THE-326's and THE-332's entries for AdminEvents.tsx and THE-342's for AdminCourses.tsx stay valid and untouched, and acceptedFor unions them. Substituting is how main went red for everyone once. NO firestore.rules digest is recorded here, deliberately and emphatically: this ticket does not touch that file, and THE-333 and THE-341 each recording one is what turned THE-325 red - THE-342 recorded that lesson and this ticket follows it, asking rulesDigestFailure() like every other pinner. NO MIGRATION WAS WRITTEN AND NO STORED DATA WAS REWRITTEN, both reported instead: the founder's $50 event still stores 50 (an edit re-writes the price it read, so an unrelated title change cannot zero it), existing registrations keep their stored amount, and the dangling adoption record is left in place - inert, since it no longer counts - and cleared, if the church chooses, through the DELETE /api/courses/adopt route that already exists and is already idempotent. adoptedCourses stays `allow write: if false`. THE-345 also appends one comment and the count 62 -> 63 to the rules-digest register suite (the one THE-325 owns) so its PINNING_SUITES stays in step with RULES_PINNERS_NOW; that file carries no ownership digest here because the register forbids naming another ticket's record in a structural field. Recorded plainly: THE-345 found TWO BROKEN GUARDS on main while doing this work and fixed both rather than leaving them. the-308-guards' 'the registration submit route is untouched' COMPARED THE FILE TO ITSELF - sha256(read(X)).toBe(sha256(read(X))) - and had protected nothing since the day it was written; it is pinned against a literal now. And AdminCourses.test.tsx's four cap tests, the guard for 'an adopted course occupies a plan slot', set mockAdopted without ever seeding mockLibrary, so every adoption in them was ITSELF A GHOST: they passed only because the cap counted raw pointers, which is the defect this ticket exists to fix. The guard for adoption was built on a fixture in which no adoption was real, so it could never have failed on a ghost, and did not. Their fixtures now seed the catalogue and the tests assert what their names say.

entries.why: THE-345 ADDS this file: the master switch for paid event ticketing, and the one function every price surface renders through. Same idiom as lib/sms-feature.ts (THE-245) and lib/stripe-connect-feature.ts (THE-256) - ONE exported boolean, and the module IMPORTS NOTHING and must not start to, because it is read from four client components and has to stay free in the bundle. It is deliberately NOT STRIPE_CONNECT_ENABLED: that flag would be true today and wrong tomorrow, because the proposition here is 'can a church be paid for a ticket at all', not 'is Stripe Connect available', and a replacement rail is being sought (Mangopay, Lemonway; card 86bbnjmw9). Gating one proposition on the other's flag would mean paid ticketing could only ever return through the rail that failed as rejected.fraud. eventPriceLabel() is ONE function for all four price surfaces on purpose: the bug was that one stored number was rendered by four independent ternaries, so gating three and missing the fourth would have left the lie in place - the same shape as the smsAvailable surface THE-335 found its sibling switch had missed. It returns null rather than 'Free' while the switch is off, because 'Free' is a different lie from '$50': the church did not decide the conference was free. csvAmountCell() reports a word rather than a figure for a non-zero stored amount, and still exports $0 for a genuinely free registration, because zero is a fact the platform can vouch for in every configuration. NO DATA IS TOUCHED BY THIS SWITCH: suppressing a QUOTE is not rewriting a FIGURE, and the founder's $50 event still stores 50.

THE-345 owns this change and it is confined to PRICE. The founder, looking at a published event reading '$50 - Registration open': 'I should not be able to create paid events with stripe disabled. How are we gonna know if someone paid or not.' Both price inputs are now ABSENT behind PAID_EVENTS_ENABLED rather than disabled-and-warning - a church that types 50 into a field that warns still expects money, which is the same lie one click further on - and an Alert stands where the event price field was, telling the church in one breath that Harvest cannot collect payments AND that registration, the QR code, check-in, the waitlist, discount codes and the CSV export are all unaffected, so it should publish, take registrations and collect at the door. handleSave's price clamp is deliberately NOT `0`: on an EDIT it re-writes the price it read, because writing a zero there would silently migrate the founder's existing $50 event the next time an admin changed its title, and zeroing stored prices is irreversible and his call. saveTicketDraft builds every NEW ticket type at 0, which rewrites nothing because stored ticketTypes arrive through openEdit untouched. The CSV Amount column reports NOT_COLLECTED_LABEL for a non-zero stored amount and still $0 for a genuinely free one. NOTHING WAS DELETED: 'Ticket Price ($)', form.price, ticketDraft.price, fmtCents and DollarSign are all still in the file and come back with the switch. NOTHING ELSE MOVED: the registration URL shape https://{tenantId}.theharvest.app/event/{eventId} is byte-identical and is asserted from the RENDERED screen; capacity, the waitlist and discount codes are untouched because they are independent of price; confirmDelete is byte-identical and handleSave moved by exactly one expression, both still pinned by region digest in the-308-guards and the-313-guards as APPENDED accepted sets; the Firestore path set is unchanged, so this ticket adds no read and no write; and THE-308's lazy month-view mount is untouched, its two files pinned by digest in this ticket's own guards.

THE-345 owns this change and it is confined to WHICH ADOPTIONS COUNT. The founder: 'In courses I only adopted one course in shadcn tenant from library but it says I used 2 in total.' An adoption POINTER whose libraryCourses document the platform had deleted was dropped from the rendered list by adoptedLibraryCourses() and still counted in adopted.length, so the header figure, both tab labels and the PLAN CAP all counted a course that does not exist and the church permanently lost a slot to it. All four now read countedAdoptions - adoptions that RESOLVE - while myAdoptedCourses stays the SEARCH-FILTERED list and is never any of them, because typing in the search box would otherwise move the figure and, through it, the cap. WHY THE POINTER DANGLES was established rather than inferred, and it is what makes the fix safe: readDocsByIds resolves ids through where(documentId(),'in',ids), which returns only documents that EXIST, so a deleted catalogue course is simply absent; a malformed pointer with no libraryCourseId is filtered out before the read. A FAILED READ CANNOT PRODUCE THE SAME SYMPTOM - readDocsByIds THROWS on a rejected chunk and never resolves into a short list - so the new adoptedResolvedKey is set ONLY on success, and a rejection leaves every figure at the raw pointer count. That is THE-342's Silent-Failure Rule applied one layer up, and it is why the cap still fails CLOSED: an unfinished or failed resolution never hands a church a slot. THE-342's work is untouched: ownCount is still the exact getCountFromServer aggregation, adopted courses still resolve BY ID, the truncation notices and the destructive read-failure Alert are unchanged, and an unknown plan still falls back to plus. This is NOT `:102`'s bug one layer down - that used the length of a CEILING-LIMITED LIST as both figure and cap input, whereas readDocsByIds is complete by construction and subject to no ceiling. A ghost is announced rather than silently rounded off, through the installed ui/alert primitive, and cleared through the EXISTING idempotent DELETE /api/courses/adopt: adoptedCourses stays `allow write: if false`, no route is added and no migration is written.

THE-345 owns this change and it is ONE price pill and one import. events/{id}.price is quoted to a member browsing a church's public calendar and charged by nothing - /api/event-registration/submit totals ticketTypes[].price and never reads it - so a member was told a conference cost $50 while the flow would have registered them free. The pill now renders through the shared eventPriceLabel(), which returns null while no rail exists, so it does not render at all; the row is already justify-between, so the register link simply sits alone. Nothing else on this screen moved: the event query, the eventUrl builder, the registration link and every other class string are byte-identical, and the stored price is untouched.

THE-345 owns this change and it is TWO price spans and one import, on the two event cards this file renders. Same defect and same fix as PublicCalendar: events/{id}.price was quoted in the member feed and charged by nothing, so both spans now render through the shared eventPriceLabel() and do not render at all while no payment rail exists. Deliberately minimal, and pinned as such: MemberScreens.desktop-layout folds exactly these two occurrences and the import in BOTH revisions, so a THIRD edit hiding behind them still fails. THE-246's onGoToPartner condition, the feed's reads, the composer, the embed cards and every other byte are untouched.

THE-345 owns this append and nothing else in the file, exactly as THE-342 owned the one before it and THE-341 the one before that. RULES_PINNERS_NOW goes 62 -> 63 and this ticket's guard suite is added to RULES_PINNERS_ADDED_SINCE beside THE-342's entry, never over it - the documented cost of adding a suite that pins firestore.rules through the shared register. No accepted value is widened, no pinner is retired, and the exact floor still may not shrink. THE-345 owns this append and nothing else in the file. ONE entry is added to RECORDED_ADOPTERS - src/components/AdminEvents.tsx, taking `alert` - because the event form needs a REPLACEMENT STATE where the Ticket Price input was: a church that came there to charge for a conference has to learn both that Harvest cannot collect the money and that registration is completely unaffected, and a heading over a silent gap would tell it neither. The entry names the primitives REJECTED and why, as every entry in that list does: `empty` announces an absent collection and this is a capability withheld over a form that is otherwise entirely usable; `badge` is a label where two sentences of instruction are needed; `field` has no control left to caption; `dialog` would interrupt a church mid-form over something it cannot change; `sonner` would leave the screen while the constraint stays; and `switch` would imply the church chooses this when the platform does. THE-308's recorded `tabs` entry is untouched, no accepted adopter is removed, and no primitive was edited - their digests are pinned elsewhere and still match.
